_description: Full researched universe of marketing/growth metric candidates (Phase 1-3). This is the research pool, NOT the build list — see calculator-catalog.json for what actually gets built. classification: calculator | calculator-educational | glossary | duplicate-variant | skip. When classification is duplicate-variant, dup names the canonical id it folds into.

candidates.name: ROAS
candidates.note: Already shipped (src/lib/calculators.ts).

candidates.name: Break-even ROAS
candidates.note: Consolidated into the Break-even Calculator (unit-economics) as a mode, not a standalone advertising page.

candidates.name: Marketing ROI
candidates.note: Already shipped. Profit-based, distinct from ROAS which is revenue-based.

candidates.name: Generic Business ROI
candidates.note: Identical formula to Marketing ROI, generic framing only.

candidates.name: CTR (ads)
candidates.note: Already shipped.

candidates.name: CPC
candidates.note: Already shipped.

candidates.name: CPM
candidates.note: Already shipped.

candidates.name: CPA
candidates.note: Same formula shape as CPC/CPM/CPL (spend/N); kept as its own page for the same named-search-term reason those already are.

candidates.name: Cost per Conversion
candidates.note: Identical formula and meaning to CPA, different label only.

candidates.name: CPL
candidates.note: Already shipped.

candidates.name: CPI (cost per install)
candidates.note: Mobile UA buying metric; same family as CPC/CPM, kept separate as its own named term.

candidates.name: CPV (cost per view)
candidates.note: Video-buying metric, same family.

candidates.name: CPE (cost per engagement)
candidates.note: Needs an explanation slot because 'engagement' means a different tracked event per platform.

candidates.name: Impression Share
candidates.note: Platform-computed from auction eligibility data the user cannot supply; not honestly calculable from a plain formula.

candidates.name: Frequency
candidates.note: Impressions/reach; distinct meaning (avg exposures per person) despite the ratio shape.

candidates.name: Reach
candidates.note: Raw platform-reported unique-user count, not derived from other inputs.

candidates.name: Video Completion Rate
candidates.note: Completions/starts.

candidates.name: Video View-Through Rate
candidates.note: Same ratio shape (views/impressions); folded in as a labeled mode.

candidates.name: Quality Score Estimate
candidates.note: Platform-proprietary black-box algorithm; a formula claiming to reproduce it would be fabricated.

candidates.name: Frequency Cap Estimate
candidates.note: Not a standardized metric; arbitrary per campaign.

candidates.name: Share of Voice
candidates.note: Own impressions/total market impressions; needs explanation because users rarely know the true denominator source.

candidates.name: Brand Lift
candidates.note: Requires survey methodology, not a formula.

candidates.name: Viewability Rate
candidates.note: Platform-measured (MRC standard), not user-computable.

candidates.name: Effective CPM (eCPM)
candidates.note: Same formula as CPM, computed post-hoc from delivered impressions.

candidates.name: Media Mix Efficiency
candidates.note: Requires MMM regression modeling, out of scope for a single-formula calculator.

candidates.name: Incremental ROAS
candidates.note: Needs a holdout-test explanation slot; formula is (test revenue - control revenue)/spend.

candidates.name: Click-to-Call Rate
candidates.note: Same ratio shape as CTR, different click target.

candidates.name: CAC
candidates.note: Already shipped.

candidates.name: Blended CAC
candidates.note: Same formula shape as CAC (spend/customers) but a different, well-known named input convention (all spend incl. $0-cost organic channels); kept separate for the same named-search-term reason as CPC/CPM.

candidates.name: Paid CAC
candidates.note: Exactly what the existing generic CAC calculator already computes when only paid spend/paid customers are entered.

candidates.name: CAC Efficiency
candidates.note: Not a standardized, single-formula metric.

candidates.name: Lead Conversion Rate
candidates.note: Same formula as the generic Conversion Rate calculator; already covered by its generic input labels.

candidates.name: Visitor-to-Lead Rate
candidates.note: Same formula as generic CR.

candidates.name: Lead-to-Customer Rate
candidates.note: Same formula as generic CR.

candidates.name: MQL-to-SQL Rate
candidates.note: B2B naming of the same ratio.

candidates.name: SQL-to-Customer Rate
candidates.note: B2B naming of the same ratio.

candidates.name: Cost per MQL
candidates.note: Same formula as CPL, B2B naming.

candidates.name: Cost per SQL
candidates.note: Same formula as CPL, B2B naming.

candidates.name: Acquisition Payback
candidates.note: Same formula as CAC Payback Period.

candidates.name: Channel CAC
candidates.note: Same formula as CAC, filtered inputs per channel, not a new formula.

candidates.name: New vs Returning Customer Ratio
candidates.note: Thin single-division utility with negligible standalone search/calculator demand.

candidates.name: AOV
candidates.note: Already shipped.

candidates.name: Revenue per Visitor
candidates.note: revenue/visitors.

candidates.name: Cart Abandonment Rate
candidates.note: Already shipped; recommend widening into a stage-labeled Abandonment Rate Calculator (see checkout-abandonment-rate).

candidates.name: Checkout Abandonment Rate
candidates.note: Same formula shape (1 - completed/started) at a different funnel stage; consolidate as a 'stage' input mode on the existing calculator instead of a new page.

candidates.name: Purchase Conversion Rate
candidates.note: Same formula as generic CR.

candidates.name: Units per Transaction
candidates.note: units/orders.

candidates.name: Repeat Purchase Rate
candidates.note: repeat customers/total customers. Cross-category duplicate of repeat-customer-rate under lifecycle-retention — see calculator-formula-families.json for the merge note.

candidates.name: Discount Rate
candidates.note: discount amount/original price.

candidates.name: Gross Margin
candidates.note: (revenue-COGS)/revenue. Shared/cross-referenced by unit-economics.

candidates.name: Contribution Margin
candidates.note: Excludes variable costs beyond COGS (shipping, payment fees); genuinely distinct from gross margin, not a duplicate.

candidates.name: Profit Margin
candidates.note: Already shipped (src/lib/calculators.ts).

candidates.name: Net Margin
candidates.note: Same formula already shipped as Profit Margin.

candidates.name: Average Basket Size
candidates.note: Alias of AOV in standard usage.

candidates.name: Revenue per Order
candidates.note: Identical formula to AOV.

candidates.name: Return Rate
candidates.note: returned units/sold units.

candidates.name: Refund Rate
candidates.note: Revenue-based counterpart to Return Rate's unit-based count; must be explicit about which base (units vs currency) is used, so kept educational rather than a silent duplicate.

candidates.name: Inventory Turnover
candidates.note: COGS/avg inventory value.

candidates.name: Gross Merchandise Value (GMV)
candidates.note: A sum, not a derived rate; no meaningful calculate step beyond addition.

candidates.name: Shipping Cost Ratio
candidates.note: shipping cost/order value.

candidates.name: Customer Concentration
candidates.note: Needs a full ranked customer list / Pareto analysis, not a single-formula input.

candidates.name: Sell-Through Rate
candidates.note: units sold/units received.

candidates.name: Price Elasticity
candidates.note: Needs multi-point regression across price changes, not a single formula.

candidates.name: Markdown Rate
candidates.note: Same formula as Discount Rate.

candidates.name: Retention Rate
candidates.note: Already shipped; recommend widening to also output Churn Rate as a second field from the same 3 inputs.

candidates.name: Churn Rate
candidates.note: Exact mathematical complement (1 - retention). Fold as a second output field, not a second page.

candidates.name: Repeat Customer Rate
candidates.note: Cross-category duplicate of the e-commerce Repeat Purchase Rate candidate — same formula, different category folder. Flagged explicitly as the Phase-3 cross-category collision example.

candidates.name: Purchase Frequency
candidates.note: Already one of the three inputs inside the LTV calculator; not a standalone tool.

candidates.name: Average Customer Lifetime
candidates.note: 1/churn rate model; needs an explanation slot because it is a modeled estimate, not an observed fact. Feeds the LTV model-variant discussion.

candidates.name: Reactivation Rate
candidates.note: reactivated/lapsed.

candidates.name: Renewal Rate
candidates.note: Subscription-context naming of the same formula; also overlaps SaaS logo-churn family.

candidates.name: Win-Back Rate
candidates.note: Alias of Reactivation Rate.

candidates.name: Dormancy Rate
candidates.note: Definition varies too much between companies (no standardized 'dormant' threshold) to ship a single correct formula.

candidates.name: Loyalty Program Participation Rate
candidates.note: enrolled members/total customers.

candidates.name: Time to Second Purchase
candidates.note: Needs a distribution/median of raw per-customer timestamps, not an aggregate-input formula.

candidates.name: Cohort Retention Curve
candidates.note: Needs a full data table input across periods; a different UI pattern than a single-formula calculator, out of scope for this phase.

candidates.name: Delivery Rate
candidates.note: delivered/sent.

candidates.name: Open Rate
candidates.note: opens/delivered.

candidates.name: Email CTR
candidates.note: Same formula shape as CTR (clicks/delivered instead of clicks/impressions); fold as a labeled mode.

candidates.name: Click-to-Open Rate (CTOR)
candidates.note: clicks/opens - a genuinely different question (content quality) than CTR (delivery+content quality combined), kept as its own tool.

candidates.name: Bounce Rate (email)
candidates.note: bounced/sent, with hard vs soft split as a validation note.

candidates.name: Unsubscribe Rate
candidates.note: unsubscribes/delivered.

candidates.name: Complaint Rate
candidates.note: spam complaints/delivered.

candidates.name: Email Conversion Rate
candidates.note: Same formula as generic CR.

candidates.name: Revenue per Recipient
candidates.note: revenue/emails sent - same family as Revenue per Visitor, cross-category family link.

candidates.name: Revenue per Email
candidates.note: Identical formula.

candidates.name: List Growth Rate
candidates.note: (new subs - unsubs)/list start.

candidates.name: Sender Reputation Score
candidates.note: ISP-proprietary, not user-computable.

candidates.name: Spam Trap Hit Rate
candidates.note: Requires external blocklist data the user cannot supply as a plain input.

candidates.name: Click-to-Conversion Rate (email)
candidates.note: Same formula as generic CR.

candidates.name: Average Emails per Conversion
candidates.note: Needs a full multi-touch attribution model; a simple ratio here would misrepresent causality.

candidates.name: Activation Rate
candidates.note: activated users/installs.

candidates.name: Install Conversion Rate
candidates.note: Store listing views to installs - same formula as generic CR.

candidates.name: DAU
candidates.note: Raw count, not a derived calculation.

candidates.name: WAU
candidates.note: Raw count.

candidates.name: MAU
candidates.note: Raw count.

candidates.name: DAU/MAU Stickiness
candidates.note: DAU/MAU - the actual derived calculator behind the raw DAU/WAU/MAU counts.

candidates.name: DAU/WAU Stickiness
candidates.note: Same ratio shape, different denominator; fold as a second output on the stickiness tool.

candidates.name: D1 Retention
candidates.note: Build as one parameterized 'N-Day Retention Calculator' with a day input, not three separate pages.

candidates.name: D7 Retention
candidates.note: Same tool, day=7.

candidates.name: D30 Retention
candidates.note: Same tool, day=30.

candidates.name: App Conversion Rate
candidates.note: Same formula as generic CR.

candidates.name: Average Session Length
candidates.note: total session duration/session count.

candidates.name: Sessions per User
candidates.note: sessions/DAU.

candidates.name: Uninstall Rate
candidates.note: uninstalls/installs.

candidates.name: Push Opt-In Rate
candidates.note: opt-ins/prompted users - same formula as generic CR.

candidates.name: ARPU (mobile)
candidates.note: Cross-category duplicate of the SaaS ARPU candidate - same formula (revenue/users).

candidates.name: ARPDAU
candidates.note: revenue/DAU - distinct daily time base from monthly ARPU; needs an explanation slot for the window difference.

candidates.name: Mobile LTV (ARPDAU model)
candidates.note: Not a new formula - a fourth LTV input-modeling convention (ARPDAU x avg lifetime days). Documented as an LTV model variant, not a new calculator.

candidates.name: Rewarded Video Completion Rate
candidates.note: Same formula as the advertising Video Completion Rate.

candidates.name: MRR
candidates.note: Sum of active subscription value. Recommend outputting ARR (x12) and MRR Growth Rate alongside it from the same tool.

candidates.name: ARR
candidates.note: MRR x 12; fold as a second output field.

candidates.name: MRR Growth Rate
candidates.note: (MRR end - MRR start)/MRR start; fold as a third output field.

candidates.name: ARPU
candidates.note: MRR/active accounts.

candidates.name: ARPA
candidates.note: Per-account vs per-user distinction only matters for multi-seat accounts; folded into ARPU as an optional 'avg seats per account' input rather than a second page.

candidates.name: Net Revenue Retention (NRR)
candidates.note: Build together with GRR as one Revenue Retention Calculator (shared inputs: starting MRR, expansion, contraction, churn).

candidates.name: Gross Revenue Retention (GRR)
candidates.note: Same input set as NRR minus the expansion term; second output of the same tool.

candidates.name: Net Dollar Retention (NDR)
candidates.note: Literal alias of NRR - important naming collision to flag explicitly.

candidates.name: Revenue Churn
candidates.note: Complement of GRR; folded into the same Revenue Retention Calculator's outputs.

candidates.name: Expansion Revenue
candidates.note: One of the Revenue Retention Calculator's input/output breakdown lines, not a standalone tool.

candidates.name: Logo Churn
candidates.note: Same formula as Churn Rate (customer count based); kept as its own SaaS-labeled page - heavily searched SaaS term, same reasoning as Blended CAC.

candidates.name: SaaS Quick Ratio
candidates.note: growth MRR/lost MRR.

candidates.name: SaaS Magic Number
candidates.note: net new ARR/prior quarter S&M spend.

candidates.name: Rule of 40
candidates.note: growth rate % + profit margin %; both must be entered as percentage points, not compounded - explicit validation rule.

candidates.name: Burn Multiple
candidates.note: net burn/net new ARR.

candidates.name: Seat Utilization Rate
candidates.note: active seats/purchased seats.

candidates.name: Trial-to-Paid Conversion Rate
candidates.note: Same formula as generic CR.

candidates.name: Free-to-Paid Conversion Rate
candidates.note: Identical formula to Trial-to-Paid, different label.

candidates.name: Annual Contract Value (ACV)
candidates.note: total contract value/contract years - per-contract, not per-account like ARPU.

candidates.name: LTV
candidates.note: Already shipped (simple model). Multiple legitimate models exist - see calculator-architecture.md Phase 5 note; do not silently pick one.

candidates.name: LTV:CAC Ratio
candidates.note: LTV/CAC - combines two existing calculators' outputs into one tool users actually want.

candidates.name: CAC Payback Period
candidates.note: CAC/(ARPU x gross margin%) - margin adjustment is a common omission error, flagged as a validation rule.

candidates.name: Break-Even Point
candidates.note: Build as one Break-Even Calculator with three outputs (break-even units, break-even CAC, break-even ROAS) from a shared margin input, not three pages.

candidates.name: Break-Even CAC
candidates.note: Second output of the Break-Even Calculator.

candidates.name: Generic Investment Payback Period
candidates.note: Same formula, generic investment framing.

candidates.name: Conversion Rate
candidates.note: Already shipped as the universal conversion-rate tool. This is the calculator every 'X-to-Y conversion rate' duplicate above folds into.

candidates.name: Funnel Conversion Rate
candidates.note: Single-step version, same formula as generic CR.

candidates.name: Multi-Step Funnel Analysis
candidates.note: Genuinely new tool: N ordered stages in, per-step conversion + overall conversion + drop-off at each stage out. Not a duplicate of the 2-input CR calculator.

candidates.name: Step Conversion Rate
candidates.note: One output row of the multi-step funnel tool.

candidates.name: Drop-off Rate
candidates.note: 1 - step conversion rate; folded into the same tool's output.

candidates.name: Form Completion Rate
candidates.note: Same formula as generic CR.

candidates.name: Field Abandonment Rate
candidates.note: Per-field, not per-form - a genuinely different question from Form Completion Rate; needs an instrumentation explanation slot.

candidates.name: Landing Page Conversion Rate
candidates.note: Same formula as generic CR.

candidates.name: Landing Page Bounce Rate
candidates.note: single-page sessions/total sessions - session-based, distinct formula shape from funnel-step abandonment.

candidates.name: Exit Rate
candidates.note: exits from page/total pageviews of that page - commonly confused with Bounce Rate, needs an explicit interpretation slot distinguishing the two.

candidates.name: Average Scroll Depth
candidates.note: Needs raw event distribution data, not an aggregate-input formula.

candidates.name: Average Time on Page
candidates.note: Simple average with thin standalone calculator demand.

candidates.name: CRO Test Velocity
candidates.note: A process metric (tests run/period), too workflow-specific to standardize as a formula.

candidates.name: Web Engagement Rate
candidates.note: Already shipped (src/lib/calculators.ts); engaged sessions/total sessions.

candidates.name: A/B Test Significance (z-test)
candidates.note: Already shipped (two-proportion z-test). Recommend adding an Absolute Uplift output field.

candidates.name: Absolute Uplift
candidates.note: variant rate - control rate; fold as an additional output field.

candidates.name: Conversion Difference
candidates.note: Literal alias of Absolute Uplift.

candidates.name: Sample Size Calculator
candidates.note: Baseline CR, MDE, power, significance -> required N per variant.

candidates.name: Minimum Detectable Effect (MDE)
candidates.note: Given N and traffic, solves for the smallest detectable effect - inverse direction of Sample Size, genuinely distinct tool.

candidates.name: Test Duration Estimator
candidates.note: required sample size/daily traffic = days needed; needs a weekly-cycle caveat (don't stop mid-week).

candidates.name: Required Runtime (weeks)
candidates.note: Same formula, different unit framing.

candidates.name: Power Analysis
candidates.note: Same underlying formula solved for a different variable; linked via relatedCalculators, not a separate page.

candidates.name: Confidence Interval Calculator
candidates.note: CI around an observed rate or an observed uplift.

candidates.name: Bayesian Probability to Beat Control
candidates.note: A second legitimate statistical method alongside the shipped frequentist z-test; document both, do not silently prefer one - Phase 5 ambiguity.

candidates.name: A/B/n Multi-Variant Significance
candidates.note: Extends the z-test with a multiple-comparison correction (e.g. Bonferroni); could become a mode of the existing tool.

candidates.name: Sample Ratio Mismatch (SRM) Check
candidates.note: Chi-square guardrail check ('is my traffic split broken') - a genuinely different question from significance testing, not a duplicate.
